texts.value: A component of desmosome cell-cell junctions which are required for positive regulation of cellular adhesion (PubMed:19717567). Promotes differentiation of keratinocytes via interaction with ERBIN. Reduces activation of RAS/ERK signaling pathways in keratinocytes via promoting ERBIN localization to the cell membrane and its interaction with SHOC2, this competitively reduces the formation of RAS-SHOC2 ERK-activating complexes (PubMed:23524970). Mediates the interaction between the desmosome and COP9 signalosome complex (CSN) protein complex (PubMed:28891468). As a result of this interaction, promotes keratinocyte differentiation via deneddylation of EGFR resulting in a reduction in EGFR protein stabilization and translocation away from the cell membrane (PubMed:28891468). Critical for epidermal integrity and barrier function of the skin (By similarity). May mediate the inflammatory response in the epidermis (By similarity). Required for esophageal epithelial barrier integrity and correct intercellular spacing in differentiated esophageal epithelium (PubMed:24220297). Required for recovery of epidermal architecture and correct expression of differentiation markers following UVB exposure (PubMed:24594668). May also be required for OCLN involvement in tight junctions (By similarity)

Monomer (PubMed:19136012). Interacts with Ca2(+); the interaction is required for the mature conformation of the protein (PubMed:12880431). Interacts (via cytoplasmic region) with JUP/plakoglobin (PubMed:19136012, PubMed:19759396). Interacts (via cytoplasmic region) with PKP1 (PubMed:19136012). Interacts with PKP2 (PubMed:11790773). Interacts (via cytoplasmic region) with DSP (via plakin domain) (PubMed:19136012). Interacts (via cytoplasmic region) with DSC1 (via cytoplasmic region) (PubMed:19136012). Interacts with DSC3; there is evidence to suggest that the interaction promotes cell-cell adhesion of keratinocytes (PubMed:19717567). Interacts (via C-terminus) with ERBIN (via C-terminus); the interaction is required for ERBIN localization to the cell membrane and keratinocyte differentiation (PubMed:23524970). The interaction also promotes ERBIN interaction with SHOC2 (PubMed:23524970). Interacts with COPS3; facilitates the interaction between the desmosome and the COP9 signalosome complex (CSN), the interaction acts to mediate EGFR signaling and keratinocyte differentiation (PubMed:28891468)
(Microbial infection) Interacts with Staphylococcus aureus protein SdrD; this interaction increases S.aureus adherence to keratinocytes

Expressed in all suprabasal layers of the epidermis, with the highest expression seen in the granular layer (at protein level) (PubMed:34905516). Expressed in the suprabasal esophageal epithelium (at protein level) (PubMed:24220297)

Protein abundance is reduced via proteasomal degradation in response to P.gingivalis infection of gingival epithelial cells (PubMed:34368962). Expression is repressed by UVB exposure, this is as a result of dissociation of the transcriptional promoter TP63 from the DSG1 upstream regulatory region (PubMed:24594668). Expression is reduced by an abundance of IL13 expression in the suprabasal esophageal epithelium (PubMed:24220297)
Three calcium ions are usually bound at the interface of each cadherin domain and rigidify the connections, imparting a strong curvature to the full-length ectodomain

(Microbial infection) Proteolytically processed by Staphylococcus aureus serine proteases eta, etb and etd (PubMed:12093888, PubMed:12880431). DSG1 is required to be bound to Ca2(+) for formation of its mature structural conformation and therefore for eta and etb cleavage (PubMed:12880431)

disease.diseaseId: Palmoplantar keratoderma 1, striate, focal, or diffuse
disease.description: A dermatological disorder characterized by thickening of the skin on the palms and soles, and longitudinal hyperkeratotic lesions on the palms, running the length of each finger.

texts.value: The disease is caused by variants affecting the gene represented in this entry. The loss of DSG1 activity results in a loss of ERBIN-mediated recruitment of SHOC2, resulting in the prevalence of SHOC2-RAS complexes and activation of ERK signaling pathways

disease.diseaseId: Erythroderma, congenital, with palmoplantar keratoderma, hypotrichosis, and hyper IgE
disease.description: A syndrome characterized by severe dermatitis, multiple allergies and metabolic wasting. Clinical features include erythroderma, yellowish papules and plaques arranged at the periphery of the palms, along the fingers and over weight-bearing areas of the feet, skin erosions and scaling, and hypotrichosis. Additionally, patients manifest severe food allergies, elevated immunoglobulin E (IgE) levels and recurrent infections with marked metabolic wasting.

texts.value: The disease is caused by variants affecting the gene represented in this entry

In Pemphigus Foliaceus (PF) patients develop an autoantibody that targets DSG1 resulting in loss of DSG1 activity (Probable). Ca2(+) is required to be bound to DSG1 for formation of its mature structural conformation and therefore for the PF autoantibody to be able to bind and inhibit DSG1 (PubMed:12880431)

In esophageal tissues of patients with eosinophilic esophagitis, mRNA transcript levels are decreased, accompanied by reduced esophageal epithelial barrier integrity and disordered intercellular spacing (PubMed:24220297). Patients with inactive eosinophilic esophagitis show normal transcript levels (PubMed:24220297)
